source.quote: ## 7. The physical error direction that closed-cycle data cannot identify
source.range_scope: Unobservable charge-error direction,installed shunt,closed-loop error budget and meter/active-noise restrictions.

source_excerpts.text:
## 7. The physical error direction that closed-cycle data cannot identify

Exact charge closure cannot be treated as a harmless implementation detail.

I constructed a counterexample: add a sufficiently slow mode whose closed-cycle covariance contribution becomes arbitrarily small while the cost of leaving a residual charge becomes arbitrarily large. The intended observable can therefore hide precisely the direction in which an imperfect pulse is expensive.

A known fixed shunt capacitor repairs that missing bound. Installing it before acquisition gives

\[
C\succeq C_{\rm sh}ee^\top,
\qquad
h(0)\le C_{\rm sh}^{-1}.
\]

The acquired law is then the law of the apparatus **with that capacitor installed**. Its addition is not assumed to preserve the earlier unprotected plant’s statistics.

I propagated charge-tracking, current, observation, and work-meter errors through the feedback loop itself. The budget includes how an error changes subsequent commands.

For the illustrative declared tolerances

\[
\varepsilon_Q=\varepsilon_I=10^{-4},
\qquad
\varepsilon_{V_m}=10^{-4},
\qquad
\varepsilon_{I_m}=10^{-5},
\]

inflating the acquisition intervals and recomputing the controller gives:

| Conditional budget term | \(k_BT\) per cell |
|---|---:|
| Rate certificate after acquisition-error inflation | 0.001372328 |
| Conservative implementation and meter penalty | 0.000787635 |
| Remaining margin | **0.000584693** |

This is an arithmetic design budget under stated error bounds. Those bounds were not measured on fabricated hardware.

In particular, a per-cell current-meter RMS specification does not establish a bound on cumulative charge drift. The charge servo and its integrated error need their own contract. The thermal shunt voltage bound also cannot be transferred unchanged to the active-noise extension.

Published electronic feedback experiments reinforce this concern: D’Urso, Odom, and Gabrielse’s electron-oscillator cooling experiment explicitly encounters amplifier heating and added feedback noise. It supports the physical feasibility of component operations while having a different plant and objective from this RC work protocol. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

## 8. Experimental evidence and comparison with strong existing methods

I applied the proposed closed integral to nine author-processed optical position records from the published Muruga data archive: **3.24 million samples at 100 Hz, totaling nine sampled hours**. Every used file was checked against its earlier byte manifest, and separate recordings were never stitched together. The archive supplies the original experimental data and analysis code. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

The descriptive training/held-out comparison was:

| Cycle duration | Training \(c_1/c_0\) | Held-out \(c_1/c_0\) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 0.4 s | −0.09286 | −0.08816 |
| 1.6 s | −0.06196 | −0.07760 |
| 6.4 s | −0.04769 | −0.06119 |

At 1.6 seconds, the individual empirical 24-cell covariance condition numbers ranged from approximately 1.51 to 1.98.

This supports investigating the observable experimentally. It does not establish the RC access contract, Gaussian stationarity, camera-noise independence, pulse tracking, or controlled work extraction. No intervention was delivered to those recorded samples.

The literature comparison also limits what can reasonably be claimed:

Established machinery	Relationship to this result
Continuous Gaussian work extraction and electrical information engines	Sandberg and collaborators already establish this operating principle and its implementation costs. Continuous work feedback itself is prior art. 
mitter.lids.mit.edu

Purified-output control	Ben-Tal, Boyd, and Nemirovski provide the established parametrization underlying response subtraction and convex synthesis. 
www2.isye.gatech.edu

Robust performance guarantees from noisy input–output data	Furieri and collaborators give a close comparator for constrained finite-horizon output feedback and suboptimality bounds. Such guarantees are not new in general. 
arxiv.org

Adaptive LQG and behavioral control	Lale and collaborators, and DeePC, already learn control from observed behavior. Their order, excitation, history, and contraction assumptions provide concrete comparisons with the specialized waveform bounds developed here. 
arxiv.org
+1

The proposed contribution is the combination of:

the physical closed-cycle observable’s uniform conditioning;
finite acquisition from a retained nonthermal state;
response acquisition through actual signed pulses;
stable sustained execution despite unresol
